subject: Business
title: Bottleneck Theory: The Weakest Link
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bottleneck Theory: The Weakest Link.

hook.text: A factory produces 100 units per hour at every station except one that does 60. Total output: 60.

buildup.text: Eliyahu Goldratt's Theory of Constraints says every system has one bottleneck that limits total throughput.

discovery.text: Improving anything except the bottleneck wastes resources. Only bottleneck improvements increase output.

twist.text: Once you fix one bottleneck, a new one appears. The system always has exactly one constraint.

climax.text: Goldratt's 'The Goal' showed that a factory doubled output by focusing on just one machine.

punchline.text: Find the bottleneck. Everything else can wait.

quiz.question: According to the Theory of Constraints, what should you improve first?
options: The single bottleneck limiting total throughput

details.summary: Bottleneck theory, derived from Eliyahu Goldratt's Theory of Constraints, states that a system's output is limited by its most constrained resource. Improving anything other than the bottleneck wastes effort because the system cannot produce more than the constraint allows.
details.whyItMatters: Most organizations improve the wrong things by optimizing non-bottleneck processes. Identifying and alleviating the true constraint produces outsized returns because every unit of improvement at the bottleneck directly increases total system output.
takeaways: System throughput is limited by the single most constrained resource
Optimizing non-bottleneck areas wastes effort and adds no output
Goldratt's five focusing steps systematically identify and resolve constraints

faq.question: How do you identify the bottleneck in a business process?
faq.answer: Look for the step with the longest queue or wait time, the resource running at full capacity while others are idle, or the process that determines the pace of the entire system. In manufacturing, it is the station with the most work-in-process inventory waiting in front of it.

faq.question: What happens after you fix a bottleneck?
faq.answer: A new bottleneck emerges elsewhere in the system because there is always a most-constrained resource. The five focusing steps are an ongoing cycle: identify the constraint, exploit it, subordinate everything to it, elevate it, then repeat. Continuous improvement is the goal.
